Owen gratefully accepts it with one hand while his other hand rests lightly over his chest; he smiles with sincere appreciation and meets her gaze. Leah smiles kindly. Leah faces him and responds warmly with an open relaxed hand, expressing 'you're welcome' and 'happy to help'. A small simple partial dining table with two used plates and two ceramic drinking glasses anchors the lower foreground; keep props minimal and realistic, no banquet or food labels. Both appear relaxed and friendly, with a clear reciprocal conversation. Transparent background outside the characters and small table.

assets.scene: Scene: Leah offers Owen a small tasteful wrapped birthday gift, soft coral paper with an ochre ribbon. Owen accepts it with visibly touched surprise and gratitude: raised eyebrows, an open delighted smile, one hand reaching to accept and the other lightly over his chest. Leah has a gentle pleased smile. A modest gift between close friends, not a romantic scene and not refusal or fear. Both sets of hands are natural and unambiguous; no party props or background. The image teaches appreciative surprise, as in 'You shouldn't have! Thank you.' without any text.

assets.scene: Scene: Owen has discovered that Leah left without telling him. Owen stands in the foreground, visibly frustrated but calm, with a disappointed furrowed brow and one open questioning palm; he holds a plain phone lowered in his other hand, its screen blank and angled away. Farther to the side Leah is in three-quarter view stepping away with a small shoulder bag, turning back with a surprised apologetic expression. Use a single coherent scene with clear spatial relationship, not split panels or duplicate characters. The poses explain why a thank-you can be sarcastic here, distinct from genuine appreciation. No exaggerated anger, no comedy sweat drops, no floating icons, no text or speech bubbles, no building or door backdrop.
